title: Build docs/spec.toml for Olympus sections 1-6 with an xtask test
summary: Rebuild the first layer of the cohesive spec (decision 3C): docs/spec.toml turns BRIEF.md 'Project Olympus' sections 1–6 (R1–R8 included) into sourced requirements, and xtask/tests/spec.rs checks it against BRIEF.md. The audience is Sri and the requirements-engineer role, who need a spec whose every line can be traced to his words by a test.

defaults_applied.how: The xtask test has negative cases and a coverage check, and cargo test and clippy must stay clean.
Criteria run the checker against the real spec and against bad specs built in memory.
Statements and decision text are written for an outside reader.
Every requirement cites verbatim quotes from BRIEF.md.
The check is a Rust test, and the data is TOML.
One focused change that covers only sections 1 to 6.
The spec carries no personal data or secrets.
The verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
Verbatim sourcing is enforced by the test.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The earlier job's one real gap, a quote checked against the whole brief rather than under its heading, is fixed here.
toml and serde are already xtask dev-dependencies, so no Cargo change is needed.
The failing athena-data test (reading_inputs_digest_is_unchanged_by_the_job_plan_section) predates this work and is out of scope.
The test reads BRIEF.md from the repository root through CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR, as policy.rs does.
The Olympus brief text is quoted word for word in BRIEF.md after line 550. Quotes come from there, and headings are those listed there (## 1. Vision through ### R8).

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/spec.toml has, for each requirement, an id, a plain cohesive statement, a kind (goal, requirement, constraint or acceptance), a status (active or superseded), and one or more sources, each a verbatim quote plus its BRIEF.md heading. It covers Olympus sections 1 to 6 and has at least one requirement for each of R1 to R8 and for sections 1 to 5.
Duplicates across the brief are merged into one requirement with several sources. Any conflict or open choice in Sri's words is recorded as an open question quoting both sides, with no resolution.
docs/decisions.md records the spec format and the choice of TOML, with alternatives. It notes that sections 7 to 10, the governing philosophy and the 2026-10-17 addenda follow in a second job.
No statement in the spec or the new test says who runs Athena or where, so xtask/tests/policy.rs still passes. No governance files change.

Run `cargo test -p xtask --test spec`. It passes on the real spec. Each in-memory negative case makes the checker fail: a quote that is not a verbatim substring of BRIEF.md after whitespace collapse, a duplicate id, a supersedes target that does not exist, and a requirement with no source. A further test fails if any of R1 to R8 or sections 1 to 5 has no requirement.
The checker also confirms each quote sits under its stated heading, not just somewhere in BRIEF.md. A negative case pairs a real quote with the wrong heading and fails. Run `cargo test -p xtask`.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean. `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` still passes.

out_of_scope: Sections 7 to 10, the governing philosophy and the addenda, which follow in a second job
Fixing the unrelated failing athena-data digest test
departures: Cost and time are raised from the reference. The spec needs reading about 250 lines of Olympus text and writing many verbatim quotes, and the previous attempt was reverted.
